verses.text: Love righteousness, you that be iudges of the earth: thinke of the Lord with a good (heart) and in simplicitie of heart seeke him.
For he will be found of them that tempt him not: and shows himself to such as do not distrust him.
For froward thoughts separate from Alahayam: and his power when it is tryed, reprooueth the vnwise.
For into a malitious soule wisedome shall not enter: nor dwell in the body that is subiect to sin.
For the holy spirit of discipline will flie deceit, & remoue from thoughts that are without understanding: and will not abide when vnrighteousnesse commeth in.
For wisedome is a louing spirit: and will not acquite a blasphemour of his words: for Alahayam is witnesse of his reines, and a true beholder of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord filleth the world: and that which containeth all things has knowledge of the voice.
Therefore he that speaks vnrighteous things, cannot be hid: neither shall vengeance, when it punisheth. passe by him.
For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words, shall come to the Lord, for the manifestation of his wicked deedes.
For the eare of iealousie heareth al things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.

Therefore beware of murmuring, which is vnprofitable, and refraine your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret that shall goe for nought: and the mouth that belieth, slayeth the soule.
Seeke not death in the errour of your life: and pull not on your selues destruction, with the workes of your hands.
For Alahayam made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthfull: and there is no poyson of destruction in them: nor the kingdome of death on the earth.
For righteousness is immortall.

But ungodly men with their workes, and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a couenant with it, because they are worthy to take part with it.

For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselues, but not aright: Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedie: neither was there any man knowen to have returned from the graue.
For we are borne at all aduenture: & we shall be heereafter as though we had never been: for the breath in our nostrils is as smoke, and a litle sparke in the mouing of our heart.
Which being extinguished, our body shall be turned into ashes, and our spirit shall vanish as the soft aire:

And our name shall be forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall passe away as the trace of a cloud: and shall be dispersed as a mist that is driuen away with the beames of the Sunne, and overcome with the heat of it.
For our time is a very shadow that passeth away: and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man commeth again.
Come on therefore, let us enioy the good things that are present: and let us speedily use the creatures like as in youth.
Let us fill our selues with costly wine, and ointments: and let no flower of the Spring passe by us.
Let us crowne our selues with Rose buds, before they be withered.
Let none of us goe without his part of our voluptuousnesse: let us leaue tokens of our ioyfulnesse in every place: for this is our portion, and our lot is this.
Let us oppresse the poore righteous man, let us not spare the widow, nor reuerence the ancient gray haires of the aged.
Let our strength be the Lawe of justice: for that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.

Therefore let us lye in wait for the righteous: because he is not for our turne, and he is cleane contrary to our doings: he vpbraideth us with our offending the Law, and obiecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
He professeth to have the knowledge of Alahayam: and he calleth himself the childe of the Lord.
He was made to reprooue our thoughts.
He is grieuous to us even to beholde: for his life is not like other mens, his waies are of another fashion.
We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthinesse: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Alahayam is his father.
Let us see if his wordes be true: and let us proue what shall happen in the end of him.
For if the just man be the son of Alahayam, he will helpe him, and deliuer him from the hand of his enemies.
Let us examine him with despitefulnesse and torrture, that we may know his meekenesse, and prooue his patience.
Let us condemne him with a shamefull death: for by his own saying, he shall be respected.
Such things they did imagine, and were deceiued: for their own wickednesse has blinded them.
As for the mysteries of Alahayam, they knew them not: neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness: nor discerned a reward for blamelesse soules.
For Alahayam created man to be immortall, and made him to be an image of his own eternitie.
Neuerthelesse through enuie of the deuill came death into the world: and they that do holde of his side do finde it.
But the soules of the righteous are in the hand of Alahayam, and there shall no torment touch them.
In the sight of the vnwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery,
And their going from us to be vtter destruction: but they are in peace.
For though they be punished in the sight of men: yet is their hope full of immortalitie.
And hauing been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Alahayam proued them, and found them worthy for himself.
As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.
And in the time of their visitation, they shall shine and runne to and fro, like sparkes among the stubble.
They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall raigne for ever.
They that put their trust in him, shall understand the truth: and such as be faithfull in love, shall abide with him: for grace & mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.
But the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken the Lord.
For who so despiseth wisedome, and nurture, he is miserable, and their hope is vaine, their labours vnfruitfull, and their works vnprofitable.
Their wiues are foolish, and their children wicked.
Their of-spring is cursed: therefore blessed is the barren that is vndefiled, which has not knowen the sinfull bed: she shall have fruit in the visitation of soules.

And blessed is the Eunuch which with his hands has wrought no iniquitie: nor imagined wicked things against Alahayam: for to him shall be given the speciall gift of faith, and an inheritance in the Temple of the Lord more acceptable to his mind.
For glorious is the fruit of good labours: and the root of wisedom shall never fall away.
As for the children of adulterers, they shall not come to their perfection, and the seed of an vnrighteous bed shall be rooted out.
For though they live long, yet shall they be nothing regarded: and their last age shall be without honour.
Or if they die quickly, they have no hope, neither comfort in the day of triall.
For horrible is the end of the vnrighteous generation.
Better it is to have no children, and to have vertue: for the memoriall of it is immortal: because it is knowen with Alahayam and with men.
When it is present, men take example at it, and when it is gone they desire it: it weareth a crown, and triumpheth for ever, hauing gotten the victorie, striuing for vndefiled rewards.
But the multiplying brood of the ungodly shall not thriue, nor take deepe rooting from bastard slips, nor lay any fast foundation.
For though they flourish in branches for a time: yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the winde: and through the force of windes they shall be rooted out.
The vnperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit vnprofitable, not ripe to eate: yea meet for nothing.
For children begotten of vnlawfull beds, are witnesses of wickednes against their parents in their triall.
But though the righteous be preuented with death: yet shall he be in rest.
For honourable age is not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of yeeres.
But wisedome is the gray haire to men, & an vnspotted life is old age.
He pleased Alahayam, and was beloued of him: so that living among sinners, he was translated.
Yea, speedily was he taken away, lest that wickednes should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soule.
For the bewitching of naughtines does obscure things that are honest: and the wandring of concupiscence, does vndermine the simple mind.
He being made perfect in a short time, fulfilled a long time.
For his soule pleased the Lord: therefore hasted he to take him away, from among the wicked.
This the people saw, and vnderstood it not: neither laid they up this in their mindes, That his grace and mercie is with his Saints, and that he has respect to his chosen.
Thus the righteous that is dead, shall condemne the ungodly, which are living, and youth that is soone perfected, the many yeeres and old age of the vnrighteous.
For they shall see the end of the wise, & shall not understand what Alahayam in his counsell has decreed of him, and to what end the Lord has set him in safetie.
They shall see him and despise him, but Alahayam shall laugh them to scorne, and they shall hereafter be a vile carkeis, and a reproch among the dead for euermore.

For he shall rend them, and cast them down headlong, that they shall be speechles: and he shall shake them from the foundation: and they shall be vtterly laid waste, and be in sorow: and their memoriall shall perish.
And when they cast up the accounts of their sins, they shall come with fear: and their own iniquities shall conuince them to their face.
Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldnesse, before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.
When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, & shall be amazed at the strangenesse of his salvation, so farre beyond all that they looked for.
And they repenting, and groning for anguish of spirit, shall say within themselues, This was he whom we had sometimes in derision, and a prouerbe of reproch.
We fooles accounted his life madnes, and his end to be without honour.
How is he numbred among the children of Alahayam, and his lot is among the Saints?
Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined to us, and the Sunne of righteousness rose not on us.
We wearied ourselues in the way of wickednesse, and destruction: yea, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of the Lord, we have not knowen it.
What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?
All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a Poste that hasted by.
And as a ship that passeth over the waues of the water, which when it is gone by, the trace of it cannot be found: neither the path way of the keele in the waues.

Or as when a bird has flowen thorow the aire, there is no token of her way to be found, but the light aire being beaten with the stroke of her wings, and parted with the violent noise and motion of them, is passed thorow, and therin afterwards no signe where she went, is to be found.
Or like as when an arrow is shot at a marke, it parteth the aire, which immediatly commeth together again: so that a man cannot know where it went thorow:
Even so we in like maner, assoone as we were borne, began to draw to our end, and had no signe of vertue to show: but were consumed in our own wickednesse.

For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blowen away with þ wind, like a thinne froth that is driuen away with þ storme: like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarieth but a day.
But þ righteous live for euermore, their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.
Therfore shall they receive a glorious kingdome, & a beautiful crowne from the Lords hande: for with his right hand shall he couer them, and with his arme shall he protect them.
He shall take to him his ielousie for cōplete armour, & make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies.
He shall put on righteousness as a brestplate, and true judgment in stead of an helmet.
He shall take holiness for an inuincible shield.
His seuere wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the vnwise.
Then shall the right-aiming thunder bolts goe abroad, and from the cloudes, as from a well-drawen bow, shall they flie to the marke.
And hailestones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stonebow, and the water of the Sea shall rage against them, & the floods shall cruelly drowne them.
Yea a mightie wind shall stand up against them, & like a storme shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay wast the whole earth, and ill dealing shall ouerthrow the thrones of the mightie.
Heare therefore, O you kings, and understand, learne you that be iudges of the ends of the earth.
Give eare you that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.
For power is given you of the Lord, & soueraigntie from the Highest, who shall try your workes; and search out your counsels.
Because being Ministers of his kingdome, you have not iudged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsell of Alahayam,
Horribly and speedily shall he come on you: for a sharpe judgment shall be to them that be in high places.
For mercy will soone pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.
For he which is Lord over all, shall fear no mans person: neither shall he stand in awe of any mans greatness: for he has made the small and great, and careth for all alike.
But a sore triall shall come on the mighty.
Unto you therefore, O kings, do I speak, that you may learne wisedome, and not fall away.
For they that keepe holiness holily, shall be iudged holy: and they that have learned such things, shall find what to answere.
Therefore set your affection on my words, desire them, and you shall be instructed.
Wisedome is glorious and never fadeth away: yea she is easily seene of them that love her, and found of such as seeke her.
She preuenteth them that desire her, in making herselfe first knowen to them.
Whoever seeks her earely, shall have no great trauaile: for he shall find her sitting at his doores.
To thinke therefore on her is perfection of wisedome: and who so watcheth for her, shall quickly be without care.
For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, shows herselfe fauourably to them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.
For the very true beginning of her, is the desire of discipline, and the care of discipline is love:
And love is the keeping of her lawes; and the giving heed to her lawes, is the assurance of incorruption.
And incorruption makes us neere to Alahayam.
Therefore the desire of wisedome bringeth to a kingdome.
If your delight be then in thrones and scepters, O you kings of the people, honour wisedome that you may raigne for euermore.

As for wisedome what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seeke her out from the beginning of her natiuity, & bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not passe over the truth.
Neither will I goe with consuming enuy: for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisedome.
But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: and a wise king is the vpholding of the people.
Receive therefore instruction thorough my words, and it shall do you good.
I my self also am a mortall man, like to all, and the ofspring of him that was first made of the earth,
And in my mothers wombe was fashioned to be flesh in the time of tenne moneths being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleepe.
And when I was borne, I drew in the common aire, and fell on the earth which is of like nature, and the first voice which I vttered, was crying as all others do.
I was nursed in swadling clothes, and that with cares.
For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.
For all men have one entrance to life, and the like going out.
Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given mee: I called on Alahayam, and the spirit of wisedome came to me.
I preferred her before scepters, and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
Neither compared I to her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and siluer shall be counted as clay before her.
I loved her above health and beautie, and chose to have her in stead of light: for the light that commeth from her never goes out.
All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.
And I reioyced in them all, because wisedome goes before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them.
I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.
For she is a treasure to men that never faileth: which they that use, become the friends of Alahayam: being commended for the gifts that come from learning.
Alahayam has granted me to speak as I would, and to conceiue as is meet for the things that are given mee: because it is he that leadeth to wisedome, and directeth the wise.
For in his hand are both we and our wordes: all wisedome also and knowledge of workemanship.
For he has given mee certain knowledge of the things that are, namely to know how the world was made, & the operation of the elements:
The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the Sunne, and the change of seasons:
The circuits of yeres, and the positions of starres:
The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wilde beasts: the violence of windes, and the reasonings of men: the diuersities of plants, and the vertues of rootes:
And all such things as are either secret or manifest: them I know.

For wisedome which is the worker of all things, taught mee: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtile, liuely, cleare, vndefiled, plaine, not subiect to hurt, louing the thing that is good, quicke, which cānot be letted, ready to do good:
Kinde to man, stedfast, sure, free from care, hauing all power, ouerseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtile spirits.
For wisedome is more moouing then any motion: she passeth and goes through all things by reason of her purenesse.
For she is the breath of the power of Alahayam, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no vndefiled thing fall into her.
For she is the brightnesse of the euerlasting light: the vnspotted mirrour of the power of Alahayam, and the Image of his goodness.
And being but one she can do all things: and remayning in her self, she makes all things new: and in all ages entring into holy soules, she makes them friends of Alahayam, & Prophets.
For Alahayam loueth none but him, that dwells with wisedome.
For she is more beautiful then the Sunne, and above all the order of starres, being compared with the light, she is found before it.
For after this commeth night: but vice shall not preuaile against wisdom.
Wisdom reacheth from one ende to another mightily: and sweetly does she order all things.
I loved her and sought her out, from my youth I dedesired to make her my spouse, and I was a louer of her beautie.
In that she is conuersant with Alahayam, she magnifieth her nobilitie: yea, the Lord of all things himself loved her.
For she is priuy to the mysteries of the knowledge of Alahayam, and a louer of his workes.
If riches be a possession to be desired in this life: what is richer then wisedome that worketh all things?
And if prudence worke; who of all that are, is a more cunning workeman then she?
And if a man love righteousness, her labours are vertues: for she teacheth temperance and prudence: justice and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in their life.

If a man desire much experience: she knows things of old, and coniectureth aright what is to come: she knows the subtilties of speaches, and can expound darke sentences: she foreseeth signes and wonders, and the euents of seasons and times.
Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with mee, knowing that she would be a counsellour of good things, and a comfort in cares & griefe.
For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honour with the Elders, though I be yong.
I shall be found of a quicke conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of great men.
When I hold my tongue they shall bide my leisure, and when I speak they shall give good eare to me: if I talke much, they shall lay their handes on their mouth.
Moreouer, by the meanes of her, I shall obtaine immortalitie, and leaue behind me an euerlasting memoriall to them that come after me.
I shall set the people in order, and the nations shall be subiect to me.
Horrible tyrants shall be afraide when they do but heare of me, I shall be found good among the multitude, and valiant in warre.
After I am come into mine house, I will repose my self with her: for her conuersation has no bitternes, and to live with her, has no sorrow, but mirth and ioy.
Now when I considered these things in my self, and pondered them in mine heart, how that to be allyed to wisedome, is immortalitie,

And great pleasure it is to have her friendship, and in the workes of her hands are infinite riches, and in the exercise of conference with her, prudence: and in talking with her a good report: I went about seeking how to take her to me.
For I was a wittie child, and had a good spirit.
Yea rather being good, I came into a body vndefiled.

Neuerthelesse when I perceiued that I could not otherwise obtaine her, except Alahayam gave her me (and that was a point of wisdom also to know whose gift she was) I prayed to the Lord, and besought him, and with my whole heart I said:
O Alahayam of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who have made all things with your word,
And ordained man through your wisedome, that he should have dominion over the creatures, which you have made,
And order the world according to equitie and righteousness, and execute judgment with an vpright heart:
Give me wisedome that sitteth by your Throne, and reiect me not from among your children:
For I your servant and son of your handmaide, am a feeble person, and of a short time, and too young for the understanding of judgment and lawes.
For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if your wisedome be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded.
You have chosen me to be a king of your people, and a Judge of your sons and daughters:
You have commaunded me to build a Temple on your holy mount, and an Altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy Tabernacle which you have prepared from the beginning:
And wisedome was with you: which knows your workes, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your Commaundements.
O send her out of your holy heavens, and from the Throne of your glory, that being present she may labour with mee, that I may know what is pleasing to you.
For she knows and vnderstandeth all things, and she shall leade me soberly in my doings, and preserue me in her power.
So shall my workes be acceptable, and then shall I judge your people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my fathers seate.
For what man is he that can know the counsell of Alahayam? or who can thinke what the will of the Lord is?
For the thoughts of mortall men are miserable, and our deuices are but vncertaine.
For the corruptible body presseth down the soule, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth on many things.
And hardly do we gesse aright at things that are on earth, and with labour do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven, who has searched out?
And your counsell who has knowen, except you give wisedome, and send your holy spirit from above?
For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you, and were saved through wisedome.
She preserued the first formed father of the world that was created alone, and brought him out of his fall,
And gave him power to rule all things.
But when the vnrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherwith he murdered his brother.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, Wisedome again preserued it, & directed the course of the righteous, in a piece of wood, of small value.

Moreouer, the nations in their wicked conspiracie being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserued him blamelesse to Alahayam, and kept him strong against his tender compassion towards his son.
When the ungodly perished, she deliuered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down on the five cities.

Of whose wickednesse even to this day the waste land that smoketh, is a testimonie, and plants bearing fruite that never come to ripenesse: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an vnbeleeuing soule.

For regarding not wisedome, they gate not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good: but also left behind them to the world a memoriall of their foolishnes: so that in the things in which they offended, they could not so much as be hid.
But Wisedome deliuered from paine those that attended on her.

When the righteous fled from his brothers wrath, she guided him in right paths: showed him the kingdome of Alahayam: and gave him knowledge of holy things, made him rich in his trauailes, and multiplied the fruit of his labours.
In the couetousnesse of such as oppressed him, she stood by him, and made him rich.
She defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait, and in a sore conflict she gave him the victory, that he might knowe that godlinesse is stronger then all.
When the righteous was solde, she forsooke him not, but deliuered him from sin: she went down with him into the pit,

And left him not in bonds till she brought him the scepter of the kingdom and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she showed them to be liers, and gave them perpetuall glory.
She deliuered the righteous people, and blamelesse seed from the nation that oppressed them.
She entred into the soule of the servant of the Lord, and withstood dreadfull kings in wonders and signes,
Rendred to the righteous a reward of their labours, guided them in a marueilous way, and was to them for a couer by day, and a light of starres in the night season:
Brought them through the red sea, and led them thorow much water.
But she drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottome of the deepe.
Therefore the righteous spoiled the ungodly, & praised your holy Name, O Lord, and magnified with one accord your hand that fought for them.
For wisedome opened the mouth of the dumbe, and made the tongues of them that cannot speak, eloquent.
She prospered their works in the hand of the holy Prophet.
They went thorough the wildernesse that was not inhabited, and pitched tents in places where there lay no way.
They stood against their enemies, and were auenged of their aduersaries.
When they were thirsty they called on you, and water was given them out of the flinty rocke, and their thirst was quenched out of the hard stone.
For by what things their enemies were punished, by the same they in their neede were benefited.
For in stead of a fountaine of a perpetuall running riuer, troubled with foule blood,
For a manifest reproofe of that commandement, whereby the infants were slaine, you gauest to them abundance of water by a meanes which they hoped not for,
Declaring by that thirst then, how you hadst punished their aduersaries.
For when they were tryed, albeit but in mercy chastised, they knew how the ungodly were iudged in wrath and tormented thirsting in another maner then the Just.
For these you did admonish, and trie as a father: but the other as a seuere king you did condemne and punish.
Whether they were absent, or present, they were vexed alike.
For a double griefe came on them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past.
For when they heard by their own punishments the other to be benefited, they had some feeling of the Lord.
For whom they reiected with scorne when he was long before throwen out at the casting forth of the infants, him in the end, when they saw what came to passe, they admired.

But for the foolish deuises of their wickednesse, wherewith being deceiued, they worshipped serpents voyd of reason, and vile beasts: you did send a multitude of vnreasonable beasts on them for vengeance,
That they might knowe that wherewithall a man sinneth, by the same also shall he be punished.
For your Almighty hand that made the world of matter without forme, wanted not meanes to send among them a multitude of Beares, or fierce Lyons,
Or unknown wild beasts full of rage newly created, breathing out either a fiery vapour, or filthy sents of scattered smoake, or shooting horrible sparkles out of their eyes:
Whereof not only the harme might dispatch them at once: but also the terrible sight vtterly destroy them.

Yea and without these might they have fallen down with one blast, being persecuted of vengeance, and scattered abroad thorough the breath of your power, but you have ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight.
For you canst show your great strength at all times when you will, and who may withstand the power of your arme?
For the whole world before you is as a litle graine of the ballance, yea as a drop of the morning dew that falleth down on the earth.
But you have mercy on all: for you canst do all things, and winkest at the sins of men: because they should amend.
For you louest all the things that are, and abhorrest nothing which you have made: for never would you have made any thing, if you hadst hated it.
And how could any thing have endured if it had not been your will? or been preserued, if not called by you?
But you sparest all: for they are your, O Lord, you louer of soules.
For your vncorruptible spirit is in all things.

Therefore chastnest you them by little, and little, that offend, and warnest them by putting them in remembrance, wherin they have offended, that leauing their wickednesse they may believe on you O Lord.
For it was your will to destroy by the handes of our fathers, both those old inhabitants of your holy land,
Whom you hatedst for doing most odious workes of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices;
And also those mercilesse murderers of children, & deuourers of mans flesh, and the feasts of blood;
With their Priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents that killed with their own hands, soules destitute of helpe:
That the land which you esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colonie of Gods children.
Neuerthelesse, even those you sparedst as men, and did send waspes forerunners of your hoste, to destroy them by little and little.
Not that you wast vnable to bring the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in battell, or to destroy them at once with cruel beastes, or with one rough word:

But executing your iudgements on them by little and little, you gauest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughtie generation, and that their malice, was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.
For it was a cursed seed, from the beginning, neither did you for fear of any man give them pardon for those things in which they sinned.

For who shall say, What have you done? or who shall withstand your judgment, or who shall accuse you for the nations that perish whom you have made? or who shall come to stand against you, to be reuenged for the vnrighteous men?
For neither is there any Alahayam but you, that careth for all, to whom you might show that your judgment is not vnright.
Neither shall king or tyrant be able to set his face against you, for any whom you have punished.
For so much then as you are righteous your self, you orderest all things righteously: thinking it not agreeable with your power to condemne him þ has not deserued to be punished.
For your power is the beginning of righteousness, and because you are the Lord of all, it makes you to be gracious to all.
For when men will not believe, that you are of a full power, you shewest your strength, and among them that know it, you makest their boldnesse manifest.
But you, mastering your power, iudgest with equitie, and orderest us with great favor: for you mayest use power when you will.
But by such workes have you taught your people, that the just man should be mercifull, and have made your children to be of a good hope, that you giuest repentance for sins.
For if you did punish the enemies of your children, and the condemned to death with such deliberation, giving them time and place, wherby they might be deliuered from their malice.
With how great circumspection diddest you judge your own sons, to whose fathers you have sworne, and made couenants of good promises?

Therefore whereas you doest chasten us, you scourgest our enemies a thousand times more, to the intent that when we judge, we should carefully thinke of your goodness, and when we our selues are iudged, we should looke for mercy.
Therefore, whereas men have lived dissolutely and vnrighteously, you have tormented them with their own abominations.
For they went astray very farre in the ways of errour, & held them for gods (which even among the beasts of their enemies were despised) being deceiued as children of no understanding.
Therefore to them, as to children without the use of reason, you did send a judgment to mocke them.
But they that would not be refourmed by that correction in which he dallied with them, shall feele a judgment worthy of Alahayam.

For looke, for what things they grudged when they were punished, (that is) for them whom they thought to be gods, being punished in them; when they saw it, they acknowledged him to be the true Alahayam, whome before they denyed to know: and therefore came extreme damnation on them.

Surely vaine are all men by nature, who are ignorant of Alahayam, and could not out of the good things that are seene, know him that is: neither by considering the workes, did they acknowledge the worke-master;
But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift aire, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven to be the gods which gouerne the world:
With whose beautie, if they being delighted, tooke them to be gods: let them know how much better the Lord of them is; for the first Author of beautie has created them.
But if they were astonished at their power and vertue, let them understand by them, how much mightier he is that made them.
For by the greatness and beautie of the creatures, proportionably the Maker of them is seene.
But yet for this they are the lesse to be blamed: for they peraduenture erre seeking Alahayam, and desirous to finde him.
For being conuersant in his workes, they search him diligently, and believe their sight: because the things are beautifull that are seene.
Howbeit, neither are they to be pardoned.
For if they were able to know so much, that they could aime at the world; how did they not sooner finde out the Lord of it?

But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who called them gods which are the workes of mens hands, golde and siluer, to shewe arte in, and resemblances of beasts, or a stone good for nothing, the worke of an ancient hand.

Now a carpenter that felleth timber, after he has sawen down a tree meet for the purpose, and taken off all the barke skilfully round about, and has wrought it handsomely, & made a vessell of it fit for the seruice of mans life:
And after spending the refuse of his worke to dresse his meat, has filled himself:

And taking the very refuse among those which serued to no use (being a crooked piece of wood, and ful of knots) has carued it diligently when he had nothing else to do, and formed it by the skill of his understanding, and fashioned it to the image of a man:
Or made it like some vile beast, laying it over with vermilion, and with paint, colouring it red, and couering every spot in it:
And when he had made a conuenient roume for it, set it in a wall, and made it fast with yron:
For he provided for it, that it might not fall: knowing that it was vnable to helpe it self, (for it is an image and has neede of helpe:)
Then makes he prayer for his goods, for his wife and children, and is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life.

For health, he calleth on that which is weake: for life, prayeth to that which is dead: for aide, humbly beseecheth that which has least meanes to helpe: and for a good iourney, he asks of that which cannot set a foot forward:
And for gaining and getting, and for good successe of his hands, asks abilitie to do, of him that is most vnable to do any thing.
Again, one preparing himself to saile, and about to passe through the raging waues, calleth on a piece of wood more rotten then the vesell that carieth him.
For verely desire of gaine deuised that, and the workeman built it by his skill:
But your prouidence, O Father, gouerneth it: for you have made a way in the Sea, and a safe path in the waues:
Shewing that you canst saue from all danger: yea though a man went to Sea without arte.
Neuerthelesse you would not that the works of your wisedome should be idle, and therefore do men commit their liues to a small piece of wood, and passing the rough sea in a weake vessell, are saved.
For in the old time also when the proud gyants perished, the hope of the world gouerned by your hand, escaped in a weake vessell, and left to all ages a seed of generation.
For blessed is the wood, whereby righteousness commeth.
But that which is made with hands, is cursed, aswell it, as he that made it: he, because he made it, and it, because being corruptible it was called Alahayam.
For the ungodly and his vngodlines are both alike hatefull to Alahayam.
For that which is made, shall be punished together with him that made it.

Therfore even on the idoles of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because in the creature of Alahayam they are become an abomination and stumbling blocks to the soules of men, and a snare to the feet of the vnwise.
For the deuising of idoles was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the inuention of them the corruption of life.
For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever.
For by the vaine glory of men they entred into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end.

For a father afflicted with vntimely mourning, when he has made an image of his childe soone taken away, now honoured him as a god, which was then a dead man, and deliuered to those that were under him, ceremonies and sacrifices.
Thus in processe of time an ungodly custome growen strong, was kept as a law, and grauen images were worshipped by the commandements of kings,

Whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt farre off, they tooke the counterfeit of his visage from farre, and made an expresse image of a king whom they honoured, to the end that by this their forwardnes, they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.
Also the singular diligence of the artificer did helpe to set forward the ignorant to more superstition.
For he peraduenture willing to please one in authoritie, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion.
And so the multitude allured by the grace of the worke, tooke him now for a god, which a litle before was but honoured as a man.
And this was an occasion to deceiue the world: for men seruing either calamitie or tyrannie, did ascribe to stones, and stockes, the incommunicable Name.
Moreouer this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of Alahayam, but whereas they lived in the great warre of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace.
For whilest they slew their children in sacrifices, or used secret ceremonies, or made reuellings of strange rites
They kept neither liues nor mariages any longer vndefiled: but either one slew another traiterously, or grieued him by adulterie:
So that there reigned in all men without exception, blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, vnfaithfulnesse, tumults, periurie,
Disquieting of good men, forgetfulnesse of good turnes, defiling of soules, changing of kinde, disorder in mariages, adulterie, and shameles vncleannesse.
For the worshipping of idoles not to be named, is the beginning, the cause, and the end of all evil.
For either they are mad when they be merry, or prophesie lies, or live vniustly, or else lightly forsweare themselues.
For insomuch as their trust is in idoles which have no life, though they sweare falsly, yet they looke not to be hurt.
Howbeit for both causes shall they be iustly punished: both because they thought not well of Alahayam, giving heed to idols, and also vniustly swore in deceit, despising holiness.
For it is not the power of them by whom they sweare: but it is the just vengeance of sinners, that punisheth alwayes the offence of the ungodly.
But you O Alahayam, are gracious and true: long suffering, and in mercy ordering all things.
For if we sin we are your, knowing your power: but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted your.
For to know you is perfect righteousness: yea to know your power is the roote of immortality.
For neither did the mischieuous inuention of men deceiue us: nor an image spotted with diuers colours, the painters fruitlesse labour.
The sight wherof entiseth fooles to lust after it, and so they desire the forme of a dead image that has no breath.
Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are louers of evil things, and are worthy to have such things to trust on.

For the potter tempering soft earth fashioneth, every vessell with much labour for our seruice: yea of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for cleane vses: and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge.

And employing his labours lewdly, he makes a vaine Alahayam of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returneth to the same out of the which he was taken: when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.

Notwithstanding his care is, not that he shall have much labour, nor that his life is short: but striueth to excel goldsmiths, and siluersmiths, and endeuoureth to do like the workers in brasse, and counteth it his glory to make counterfeit things.
His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile then earth, and his life of lesse value then clay:
Forasmuch as he knew not his maker, and him that inspired into him an actiue soule, and breathed in a living spirit.
But they counted our life a pastime, & our time here a market for gaine: for, say they, we must be getting every way, though it be by euil meanes.
For this man that of earthly matter makes brickle vessels, and grauen images, knows himself to offend above all others.
And all the enemies of your people, that hold them in subiection are most foolish and are more miserable then very babes.

For they counted all the idoles of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor eares to heare, nor fingers of hands to handle, and as for their feete they are slow to goe.
For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them, but no man can make a god like to himself.
For being mortall he worketh a dead thing with wicked hands: for he himself is better then the things which he worshippeth: whereas he lived once, but they never.
Yea they worshipped those beasts also that are most hatefull: for being compared together, some are worse then others.
Neither are they beautifull, so much, as to be desired in respect of beasts, but they went without the praise of Alahayam and his blessing.
Therefore by the like were they punished worthily, and by the multitude of beasts tormented.
In stead of which punishment, dealing graciously with your own people you preparedst for them meate of a strange taste: even quailes to stirre up their appetite:

To the end that they desiring food might for the ougly sight of the beasts sent among them, loath even that which they must needs desire: but these suffering penury for a short space, might be made partakers of a strange taste.
For it was requisite, that on them excercising tyranny should come penury which they could not auoyde: but to these it should only be showed how their enemies were tormented.
For when the horrible fiercenesse of beasts came on these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, your wrath endured not for ever.
But they were troubled for a smal season that they might be admonished, hauing a signe of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandement of your Law.
For he that turned himself towards it, was not saved by the thing that he saw: but by you that are the savior of all.
And in this you madest your enemies confesse, that it is you who deliuerest from all evil:
For them the bitings of grassehoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such.
But your sons, not the very teeth of venemous dragons ouercame: for your mercy was ever by them, and healed them.
For they were pricked, that they should remember your words, and were quickly saved, that not falling into deep forgetfulnesse, they might be continually mindefull of your goodness.
For it was neither herbe, nor mollifying plaister that restored them to health: but your word, O Lord, which healeth all things.
For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.
A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit when it is gone foorth returneth not; neither the soule received up, commeth again.
But it is not possible to escape your hand.

For the ungodly that denied to know you, were scourged by the strength of your arme: with strange raines, hailes, and showers were they persecuted, that they could not auoyd, and through fire were they consumed.
For, which is most to be wondered at, the fire had more force in the water that quencheth all things: for the world fighteth for the righteous.

For sometimes the flame was mitigated, that it might not burne up the beasts that were sent against the ungodly: but themselues might see and perceiue that they were persecuted with the judgment of Alahayam.
And at another time it burneth even in the midst of water, above the power of fire, that it might destroy the fruits of an vniust land.
In stead whereof you feddest your own people, with Angels food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every mans delight, and agreeing to every taste.
For your sustenance declared your sweetnesse to your children, and seruing to the appetite of the eater tempered it self to every mans liking.
But snow and yce endured the fire and melted not, that they might know that fire burning the haile, and sparkling in the raine, did destroy the fruits of the enemies.
But this again did even forget his own strength, that the righteous might be nourished.
For the creature that serueth you who are the maker, encreaseth his strength against the vnrighteous for their punishment, and abateth his strength for the benefit of such as put their trust in you.
Therefore even then was it altered into all fashions, and was obedient to your grace that nourisheth all things, according to the desire of them that had need:
That your children, O Lord, whom you louest, might know that it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man: but that it is your word which preserueth them that put their trust in you.
For that which was not destroied of the fire, being warmed with a litle Sunne beame, soone melted away,
That it might be knowen, that we must preuent the Sunne, to give you thanks, and at the day-spring pray to you.
For the hope of the vnfaithfull, shall melt away as the Winters hoarefrost, and shall runne away as vnprofitable water.
For great are your Iudgements, and cannot be expressed: therefore vnnourtured soules have erred.

For when vnrighteous men thought to oppresse the holy nation: they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, and fettered with the bondes of a long night, lay exiled from the eternall prouidence.
For while they supposed to lie hid in their secret sins, they were scattered under a darke vaile of forgetfulnesse, being horribly astonished, and troubled with (strange) apparitions.
For neither might the corner that helde them keepe them from fear: but noises (as of waters) falling down, sounded about them, and sadde visions appeared to them with heauie countenances.
No power of the fire might give them light: neither could the bright flames of the starres endure to lighten that horrible night.
Only there appeared to them a fire kindled of it self, very dreadfull: for being much terrified, they thought the things which they saw to be worse then the sight they saw not.
As for the illusions of arte Magicke, they were put down, and their vaunting in wisedome was reprooued with disgrace.
For they that promised to driue away terrours, and troubles from a sicke soule, were sicke themselues of fear worthy to be laughed at.
For though no terrible thing did fear them: yet being skared with beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents,
They died for fear, denying that they saw the ayre, which could of no side be auoided.
For wickednesse condemned by her own witnesse, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, alwayes forecasteth grieuous things.
For fear is nothing else, but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.
And the expectation from within being lesse, counteth the ignorance more then the cause which bringeth the torment.
But they sleeping the same sleepe that night which was indeed intolerable, and which came on them out of the bottomes of ineuitable hell:
Were partly vexed with monstrous apparitions, and partly fainted, their heart failing them: for a suddaine fear and not looked for, came on them.
So then, whoever there fell down, was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without yron barres.

For whether he were husbandman, or shepheard, or a labourer in the field, he was ouertaken, and endured that necessitie, which could not be auoided: for they were all bound with one chaine of darkness.
Whether it were a whistling winde, or a melodious noise of birdes among the spreading branches, or a pleasing fall of water running violently:

Or a terrible sound of stones cast down, or a running that could not be seene of skipping beasts, or a roaring voice of most sauage wilde beasts, or a rebounding Eccho from the hollow mountaines: these things made them to swoone for fear.
For the whole world shined with cleare light, and none were hindered in their labour.
Over them only was spread an heauie night, an image of that darkness which should afterwards receive them: but yet were they to themselues more grieuous then the darkness.
Neuerthelesse, your Saints had a very great light, whose voice they hearing and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy.
But for that they did not hurt them now, of whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, and besought them pardon, for that they had been enemies.
In stead whereof you gauest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown iourney, and an harmelesse Sunne to entertaine them honourably.
For they were worthy to be depriued of light, and imprisoned in darknesse, who had kept your sons shut up, by whom the vncorrupt light of the law was to be given to the world.

And when they had determined to slay the babes of the Saints, one child being cast forth, and saved: to reproue them, you tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mightie water.
Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing to what oathes they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheere.
So of your people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.
For wherewith you did punish our aduersaries, by the same you did glorifie us whom you hadst called.

For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy lawe, that the Saints should be alike partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise.
But on the other side there sounded an ill-according crie of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was caried abroad for children that were bewailed.
The master and the seruaunt were punished after one maner, and like as the king, so suffered the common person.
So they altogether had innumerable dead with one kind of death, neither were the living sufficient to burie them: for in one moment the noblest ofspring of them was destroyed.
For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments, on the destruction of the first borne, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of Alahayam.
For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course,
Your almighty word leapt down from heaven, out of your royall throne, as a fierce man of warre into the midst of a land of destruction,
And brought your vnfained commandement as a sharpe sword, and standing up filled all things with death, and it touched the heaven, but it stood on the earth.
Then suddenly visions of horrible dreames troubled them sore, and terrours came on them vnlooked for.
And one throwen here, another there halfe dead, showed the cause of his death.
For the dreames that troubled them, did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.
Yea, the tasting of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wildernes: but the wrath endured not long.

For then the blamelesse man made haste, and stood foorth to defend them, and bringing the shield of his proper ministerie, even prayer and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your servant.
So he ouercame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of armes, but with a word subdued he him that punished, alleaging the oathes and couenants made with the fathers.
For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one on another, standing between, he staied the wrath, and parted the way to the living.
For in the long garment was the whole world, & in the four rowes of the stones was the glory of the fathers grauen, and your maiestie on the diademe of his head.
To these the destroyer gave place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.
As for the ungodly, wrath came on them without mercie to the end: for he knew before what they would do;
Howe that hauing given them leaue to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them.
For whilest they were yet mourning, and making lamentation at the graues of the dead, they added another foolish deuice, and pursued them as fugitiues, whom they had entreated to be gone.

For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them to this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfill the punishment which was wanting to their torments,
And that your people might passe a wonderfull way: but they might find a strange death.
For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, seruing the peculiar commandements that were given to them, that your children might be kept without hurt.
As namely, a cloud shadowing the campe, and where water stood before drie land appeared, and out of the red Sea a way without impediment, and out of the violent streame a greene field:
Where-thorough all the people went that were defended with your hand, seeing your marueilous strange wonders.
For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambes, praising you O Lord, who hadst deliuered them.

For they were yet mindefull of the things that were done while they soiourned in the strange land, how the ground brought forth flies in stead of cattell, and how the riuer cast up a multitude of frogs in stead of fishes.
But afterwards they saw a new generation of foules, when being led with their appetite they asked delicate meates.
For quailes came up to them from the Sea, for their contentment.

And punishments came on the sinners not without former signes by the force of thunders: for they suffered iustly, according to their own wickednesse, insomuch as they used a more hard and hatefull behauiour towards strangers:
For the Sodomits did not receive those whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserued of them.
And not only so: but peraduenture some respect shall be had of those, because they used strangers not friendly.
But these very grieuously afflicted them, whom they had received with feastings, and were already made partakers of the same lawes with them.

Therefore even with blindnesse were these stricken, as those were at the doores of the righteous man: when being compassed about with horrible great darknesse, every one sought the passage of his own doores.

For the elements were changed in themselues by a kind of harmonie, like as in a Psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are alwayes sounds, which may well be perceiued by the sight of the things that have been done.
For earthly things were turned into watry, and the things that before swamme in the water, now went on the ground.
The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own vertue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature.
On the other side, the flames wasted not the flesh of the corruptible living things, though they walked therin, neither melted they the ycie kind of heauenly meate, that was of nature apt to melt.
For in all things, O Lord, you did magnifie your people, and glorifie them, neither did you lightly regard them: but did assist them in every time and place.
